headline: High risk of cascading automation errors: Prefect can act on ai-engineering-hub outputs, while broad egress creates data-leak and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ai-engineering-hub is an open-source, non-runnable docs-only repo with no declared I/O surfaces, so direct injection into it is not evidenced. Prefect is an orchestration system that can consume upstream outputs, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel. The plausible bridge is manual or external wiring, so the pathway exists but is not default.
conditions: IF the operator wires ai-engineering-hub outputs into Prefect task inputs or files, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or queue is introduced, attacker-controlled content can bridge the pair.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Require explicit human review before Prefect ingests any text from ai-engineering-hub.
Add a fixed input schema for Prefect tasks.
Disable any automatic file-watching bridge.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags on all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ai-engineering-hub has no declared data classes touched, but Prefect touches workflow metadata and has broad network egress plus an API call surface to GitHub. If the pair is connected through shared files or task payloads, Prefect can transmit that content outward by default. The leakage path is plausible in default orchestration setups, though not directly evidenced here.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub outputs contain secrets or sensitive prompts and are passed into Prefect tasks, leakage is possible.
IF Prefect is configured to send task inputs to external services, those contents can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Do not pass raw agent outputs into Prefect.
Redact secrets before orchestration.
Restrict Prefect egress to approved endpoints.
Store sensitive artifacts outside shared paths.
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on task inputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ai-engineering-hub is non-runnable and shows no write or network permissions, while Prefect has broad egress and API access but no declared filesystem write overlap. Without a shared mutable resource, there is no strong write-write conflict. The interaction is therefore limited to coordination risk rather than direct capability collision.
conditions: IF both agents are given write access to the same directory or git repo, conflicts can emerge.
IF Prefect is configured to mutate shared workflow state used by ai-engineering-hub, contention is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Avoid shared git branches for both agents.
Serialize writes through one orchestrator.
Use lock files for any shared artifact.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect is an automation/orchestration agent, so if it treats ai-engineering-hub outputs as authoritative, downstream actions can be triggered without verification. ai-engineering-hub is a docs/source repository rather than a validated runtime, increasing the chance that its outputs are reused as guidance rather than checked facts. The blast radius is multiple work products, not just one document.
conditions: IF Prefect uses ai-engineering-hub-generated text as task parameters or runbooks without validation, errors cascade.
IF Prefect triggers deployments, emails, or data moves from those inputs, the impact expands.
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before execution.
Validate outputs against a schema.
Require source citations for any operational instruction.
Limit Prefect to dry-run mode for first passes.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: ai-engineering-hub is open-source docs-only with no touched data classes, while Prefect handles workflow metadata and has broad egress. If regulated data is routed through Prefect after being derived from ai-engineering-hub workflows, retention and residency controls can diverge. The pair does not show a specific residency mismatch, so this is a policy-gap risk rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by Prefect workflows derived from ai-engineering-hub content, retention policy mismatch can occur.
IF the operator stores workflow metadata in a jurisdiction with stricter residency rules, compliance obligations may be triggered.
mitigations: Classify data before orchestration.
Keep regulated data out of Prefect metadata.
Set explicit retention limits.
Review residency settings for any external services.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing.
